entities.name: GlmU
observations: The 466-residue query protein is a strong homolog of reviewed bacterial bifunctional GlmU proteins, with 41.5–44.9% identity and 94.6–97.9% query coverage.
GlmU catalyzes the final two reactions of UDP-N-acetylglucosamine biosynthesis.
The N-terminal region is a nucleotide-transfer/pyrophosphorylase module; the C-terminal region is a Hexapep-associated N-acetyltransferase module, separated by a linker near residues 230–251.
Reference GlmU proteins are cytoplasmic homotrimers and bind one Mg2+ ion per subunit.

entities.name: GlcN-1-P acetylation
observations: Glucosamine-1-phosphate + acetyl-CoA → N-acetylglucosamine-1-phosphate + CoA + H+; associated with EC 2.3.1.157 and Rhea RHEA:13725.
This reaction is catalyzed by the C-terminal N-acetyltransferase domain of GlmU.

entities.name: UDP-GlcNAc formation
observations: N-acetylglucosamine-1-phosphate + UTP + H+ → UDP-N-acetylglucosamine + diphosphate; associated with EC 2.7.7.23 and Rhea RHEA:13509.
This reaction is catalyzed by the N-terminal pyrophosphorylase domain of GlmU and requires Mg2+.

entities.name: UDP-GlcNAc biosynthesis
observations: GlmU performs the final two sequential steps in bacterial UDP-N-acetylglucosamine biosynthesis, supporting peptidoglycan and, in relevant bacteria, lipid A biosynthesis.
